raw_text: Bangladesh shuts down internet as student protests turn deadly. Bangladesh has shut down mobile internet services across the country as student-led protests against the government's quota system for civil service jobs turned violent, killing at least six people. The demonstrations, which began last week at universities in Dhaka, have spread across the country with tens of thousands taking to the streets. Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's government deployed paramilitary forces after police failed to contain the protests. Students are demanding the abolition of a system that reserves more than half of government jobs. The internet shutdown has made it difficult to verify reports from outside Dhaka. India is monitoring the situation closely given concerns about potential refugee flows across the border.
